links.outcome: Readability grade level of LLM patient education responses versus AMA/NIH recommended sixth-to-eighth grade
links.effect: No model consistently met sixth-to-eighth grade levels; OpenEvidence was at or above 17th grade, while ChatGPT and Gemini averaged 11.9-12.0 grade.
links.quote: No model consistently met the American Medical Association (AMA)/National Institutes of Health (NIH)-recommended reading levels for sixth through eighth grade.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education material relative to recommended level
links.effect: All three LLMs produced content above recommended reading levels; OpenEvidence was at or above 17th grade (postbaccalaureate), ChatGPT and Gemini about 12th grade.
links.quote: No model consistently met the American Medical Association (AMA)/National Institutes of Health (NIH)-recommended reading levels for sixth through eighth grade.

links.outcome: Day-to-day consistency (Jaccard similarity) of LLM responses to identical questions
links.effect: ChatGPT was most stable (range <0.07), Gemini moderately variable, OpenEvidence had the widest range (0.24) and highest average similarity (0.383).
links.quote: ChatGPT showed the highest day-to-day stability (range: <0.07), Gemini moderate variability, and OpenEvidence both the widest range (0.24) and the highest average similarity (0.383).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM-generated patient education content across readability, accuracy, and consistency without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
